letter_markdown:
# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** UnitedHealthcare / Oxford — Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter dated 2026-08-16]

**From:** Cameron Carter
Member ID: W300143742
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-16 — Reference number POC-3469ABE4FC-29435**
**Service denied:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
**Plan:** UnitedHealthcare / Oxford (Commercial/ACA), New Jersey
**Governing policy:** *Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O)* — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/surgery-ankle.pdf

---

## 1. What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the prior authorization request for my total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). The notice dated 2026-08-16 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that determination and to approve the surgery. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records submitted with the prior authorization request support that.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in my denial notice, which says the appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-12**. To make sure it reaches the right place, I am filing it through my online member account at member.uhc.com, calling the number on my member ID card if I need help doing so, and sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial notice.

## 2. The plan's own policy, and how my records match it

The plan's policy *Surgery of the Ankle (2026T0622O)* states:

> "Coverage Rationale Surgery of the ankle is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances."

So ankle surgery is not excluded under my plan. The question is only whether my particular circumstances meet the clinical criteria. Here is what my records show:

- **Duration and failure to improve with time and rest.** I have had 9 months of progressive pain in the ankle, unrelieved by rest.
- **Supervised conservative care, completed and documented.** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance — 16 weeks, from 2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trials, also failed.** I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief. I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-14, which gave 4 weeks of partial relief and then wore off.
- **Objective imaging.** Weight-bearing ankle radiographs on 2026-06-28 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts.
- **Objective exam findings.** I have positive provocative testing on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.
- **Functional loss.** I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks.
- **Surgical candidacy.** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

The plan's policy also states:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I understand that submitting records does not by itself guarantee coverage. I am pointing to the specific contents of those records above, because they speak directly to the things a medical necessity review of a joint replacement would look at: how long the problem has lasted, what non-surgical treatment was tried and for how long, what the imaging shows, and how much function has been lost.

## 3. The one thing this policy calls unproven is not my procedure

The policy contains a specific "unproven" statement, and it is about a different operation than mine:

> "Osteochondral allograft or autograft transplant is unproven and not medically necessary for treating cartilage defects of the ankle due to insufficient evidence of efficacy."

The surrounding discussion in the policy is likewise about that procedure — for example:

> "however, a considerable number of the allografts failed, requiring repeat allografting, arthrodesis, or arthroplasty (range, 11%-48%)."

and

> "All studies exhibited a high risk of bias in at least one domain, with 64% demonstrating a high risk across at least four domains."

and

> "Clinical Practice Guidelines American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) The AOFAS (2022) published a position statement that supports the use of osteochondral autograft and allograft transplant for the treatment of OLTs that have failed nonsurgical management, especially for large-diameter lesions, cystic lesions, and lesions that have failed previous surgical treatment."

I am not requesting an osteochondral allograft or autograft transplant. I am requesting a total ankle replacement, CPT 27702. I would ask the reviewer to confirm that the "unproven" finding in this policy was not applied to my request.

## 4. The criteria used to deny me were not given to me

For the medical necessity rules themselves, the policy does not spell them out. It points elsewhere:

> "For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the InterQual® CP:"

> "Arthrodesis, Ankle (Talotibial Joint) Arthroscopy, Surgical, Ankle Arthrotomy, Ankle Total Joint Replacement (TJR), Ankle Click here to view the InterQual® criteria."

> "UnitedHealthcare may also use tools developed by third parties, such as the InterQual® criteria, to assist us in administering health benefits."

I want to be straightforward about this: **I have not been able to quote the specific clinical threshold my request was measured against, because the plan has not provided it.** InterQual is licensed software, not a public document, so I cannot look it up myself. I am not going to guess at what it requires, and I would ask that no reviewer assume I have conceded any threshold I have not seen.

## 5. Request for the criteria relied upon (please respond in writing)

**I am formally requesting, free of charge and in writing, the specific rule, guideline or criterion relied upon in denying my request — specifically, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**, along with the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination. Federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules entitle me to the specific rule or criterion relied on for an adverse benefit determination. Once I receive that criteria text, I ask that I be given the opportunity to respond to it as part of this appeal, and that my surgeon be permitted to supply any additional documentation the criteria call for.

## 6. What I am asking the plan to do

Please overturn the denial issued 2026-08-16 (reference POC-3469ABE4FC-29435) and authorize the total ankle replacement, CPT 27702, as requested by Dr. Lindqvist. In the alternative, please provide the InterQual criteria applied to my case and identify precisely which element my documentation did not satisfy, so that it can be addressed.

If any part of this appeal is incomplete, please contact me rather than closing the file. I am also requesting a copy of my full claim file and all documents relevant to this determination. If this appeal is not approved, please tell me in writing how to request an external review.

Thank you for taking another look at this. I am in pain every day, I can walk about two blocks, and I have done everything my care team asked of me before surgery was proposed.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Carter**
Member ID: W300143742
Reference number: POC-3469ABE4FC-29435
[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-16
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-03-13 to 2026-07-03, 24 visits)
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report dated 2026-06-28
- Office and operative-planning notes from Dr. Lindqvist, MD
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-04-14)
- [Any other records my surgeon's office is submitting]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
